title: Undo and redo for a text editor

task.text: Make each edit an object that can run itself and take itself back.
`Doc` and `Command` are given. Implement the **command** pattern in `Editor.java`.

items: `Insert(Doc doc, int at, String s)` inserts `s` at `at`; its undo removes it.
`Delete(Doc doc, int from, int to)` removes `[from, to)`; its undo puts the removed text back. It must remember the text each time it executes.
`History`: `run(Command)` executes and records; `undo()` and `redo()` step back and forward; `canUndo()` and `canRedo()` report. Undo or redo with nothing to do is a no-op.
Running a new command discards the redo list.

checks.title: Inserts can be undone one by one
Undoing a delete restores the text
Redo replays undone commands in order
Delete recaptures the text on every execute
A new command clears the redo list
An empty History ignores undo and redo
History drives a Command it has never seen
History never mentions Doc, Insert or Delete
Insert and Delete hold their Doc

hints.text: A request becomes an object that carries everything needed to do it and to reverse it. The caller that runs and remembers requests then needs no knowledge of what they do.
`Insert` and `Delete` keep a `final Doc` and their arguments. `Delete.execute` stores what `doc.delete` returns. `History` keeps two stacks of `Command`: done and undone.
